proposal.name: wider_window_4s
proposal.rationale: The dominant error is steady_confusion (88.8% of error rows, whole-segment misclassification, not boundary lag), and the population's slow-cadence tail (down to 0.13 Hz per DOMAIN NOTES §9) means a 2s window often spans under one full stride, giving noisy amplitude/correlation estimates that RF misreads for an entire segment; a 4s window covers full gait cycles on slow walkers (plausibly rev14, the worst per-rev score at 0.61) at the cost of more abstention only at transitions, which are already a small minority of total error.

reasons: Not a repeat: ledger only has baseline (2s, implicit) and drop_absolute_angle (also 2s); no prior window_s experiment exists.
Single-variable change: only window_s modified, drop_features and model_params empty — clean attribution.

Targets the dominant bucket: steady_confusion is 88.8% of error rows, and the mechanism (partial-stride 2s windows on slow-cadence gait producing noisy features that RF misreads for a whole segment) plausibly explains whole-segment misclassification, unlike transition-only fixes.

Consistent with DOMAIN NOTES §9, which explicitly flags window length as an open tradeoff and states 4s is needed for slow gait at the cost of more transition abstention — this is exactly what's proposed, not a contradiction of any established finding.

rev14 slow-cadence claim is appropriately hedged ('plausibly') rather than asserted as confirmed, avoiding overclaiming beyond what champion report shows (rev14 is worst-scoring rev, consistent but not proof of cadence cause).

reasons: Novel: no ledger entry touches band_frac/gait-band features (baseline, drop_absolute_angle, wider_window_4s, window_4s_stride_2s all target different fields)

Mechanism is grounded directly in DOMAIN NOTES §9 (0.5-3.0Hz band is wrong for a population with cadence down to 0.13Hz) rather than contradicting it

proposal.name: regularize_min_samples_leaf10
proposal.rationale: The dominant error bucket, steady_confusion (88.8% of error rows), is whole-segment misclassification under leave-one-rev-out CV, i.e. a generalization failure across subjects rather than a boundary/lag issue, and unconstrained trees (default min_samples_leaf=1) can carve leaves around training-rev-specific quirks (per-file offsets/calibration per DOMAIN NOTES SS7) that fail to transfer to a held-out rev like rev14 (0.61 F1, the worst); raising min_samples_leaf to 10 forces splits to rely on patterns shared across multiple subjects instead of memorizing single-rev idiosyncrasies.

reasons: Novel: no ledger entry touches model_params/regularization; all prior tests changed features or window_s, not tree complexity.
Single change (min_samples_leaf 1->10), cleanly attributable.

Targets the dominant error bucket (steady_confusion, 88.8%) via a plausible mechanism: whole-segment misclassification concentrated on worst-generalizing rev14 (0.61) is consistent with unconstrained leaves memorizing per-rev idiosyncrasies rather than a boundary/lag artifact.
Does not contradict DOMAIN NOTES dead ends (signal-based sagittal detection, naive decimation) or any §7/§9 finding.

Caveat, not disqualifying: drop_absolute_angle already targeted the same 'per-file calibration leaks into training' theory directly and only gained +0.0028, so the calibration-overfit story has shown limited leverage before -- worth flagging in the report writeup, but min_samples_leaf regularizes overfitting generally (not just via those features), so it's a distinct enough mechanism to still be worth the run.

Targets the dominant error bucket (steady_confusion, 88.8% of error rows) via a stated, plausible mechanism: RF's per-split feature subsampling can build leaves on a zero-signal feature, encoding per-rev stance idiosyncrasies that don't generalize under leave-one-rev-out CV
Consistent with DOMAIN NOTES §10.1, which directly measured interleg_offset at AUC 0.50 for walk/stand (posture-only) — no contradiction

reasons: False premise (check 0): rationale claims 'unweighted RF splits are dominated by walk-majority votes' and frames class_weight as 'an axis never yet tested', but stages/s2_ml/experiment.py:31-32 (BASE_MODEL_PARAMS) and stages/s2_ml/train.py:33 already hard-code class_weight='balanced' for every experiment run to date, including the current champion.

Not a repeat: drop_bad_band_frac (rejected, -0.0019) dropped the sibling _spectral() output (band_frac) on a 'reads near-zero for slow walkers' argument; this targets dom_hz specifically on a distinct mechanism (coarse-bin quantization causing rev-identifying leakage under LORO), not the same claim restated.
Single conceptual change (drop one descriptor, both sides), consistent with the L/R-pair granularity already accepted in drop_offset_only and drop_bad_band_frac.
Targets steady_confusion, the dominant bucket (82% of error rows), satisfying the leverage check on bucket size.

Caveat, not disqualifying: L/R_angvel_dom_hz don't appear in the champion report's top-12 feature importances (cumulative ~0.856), suggesting modest average split usage — weakens confidence the mechanism is a major driver, but low aggregate importance doesn't rule out rev-specific overfitting on a handful of splits, so this is worth letting the gate settle rather than pre-judging.

No contradiction with DOMAIN NOTES; per §11.4, remember the gate will only confirm the metric, not this leakage story — don't promote the rationale into DOMAIN_NOTES on the strength of a macro-F1 move alone.

proposal.name: drop_ang_mean_only
proposal.rationale: L_ang_LPF_mean and R_ang_LPF_mean are dominated by each window's static angle bias, which §4.6 identifies as a firmware/mounting zeroing convention baked into the on-sensor Deg fusion rather than gait content, and §10.1 already showed the analogous relative-bias feature (ang_LR_offset, AUC 0.50) was pure per-rev posture noise whose removal cut steady_confusion and promoted the champion; the absolute per-side mean is the same kind of static-offset signal one level down, so isolating it (unlike drop_absolute_angle, which diluted the effect by bundling mean with absmean and offset together for only +0.0028) should further reduce the still-dominant steady_confusion bucket (0.820 share) without touching the amplitude/correlation features that actually carry gait information.

reasons: Premise verified in stages/s2_ml/features.py:86: `{name}_mean` is the per-window arithmetic mean of L_ang_LPF/R_ang_LPF, i.e. the window's absolute sagittal-angle level — consistent with the rationale's claim that it reflects per-file/per-rev zeroing rather than gait dynamics (amplitude/shape features like _std/_ptp/_ang_LR_corr are untouched).

§4.6 supports the generalization: Deg is on-sensor fusion whose 'fusion parameters are a device property' that can differ by revision even with matching column names — legitimately extends the zeroing-convention argument from Hip_Deg to L/R_ang_LPF_mean.

Not a repeat: drop_absolute_angle (rejected, +0.0028) bundled this with absmean and ang_LR_offset and was explicitly diagnosed as diluted; this isolates the untested remainder (mean-only) exactly the way drop_offset_only isolated ang_LR_offset from the same bundle and got promoted — same de-confounding logic, different feature subset, run against the current champion (post offset-drop, post dom_hz-drop), so it's not stale.
Single conceptual change (L/R pair of one feature type dropped together), consistent with precedent (drop_angvel_dom_hz also dropped an L/R pair as one change).
Targets the dominant error bucket (steady_confusion, 0.820 share) per rule 3.

Caveat for the log, not a blocker: L_ang_LPF_mean/R_ang_LPF_mean don't appear in the top-12 importance list for the current champion, so raw RF importance is low; per §11.4 the mechanism (steady_confusion reduction) must actually be checked against the taxonomy output regardless of whether macro-F1 moves, not assumed from the rationale.

proposal.name: max_features_full_split
proposal.rationale: Default RandomForest max_features='sqrt' considers only ~4 of the champion's 18 surviving features at every split, a heuristic sized for hundreds-of-features problems; with just 18 features (after the promoted static-offset-family drop) that starves root-level splits of the dominant discriminators (ang_LR_corr, L/R_ang_LPF_std/ptp, all top-5 importance) some fraction of the time, so different bootstrap trees anchor their early structure on whichever weaker feature got sampled instead of the strongest one, plausibly producing the whole-segment, non-reversing steady_confusion errors (82% of error rows) rather than boundary noise; setting max_features=None lets every split see the full feature set, and this direction is consistent with min_samples_leaf=10 (more regularization) having already cost -0.0549 on this same dominant bucket, i.e. this pipeline currently favors less-constrained trees, not more.

Not a repeat: no ledger entry touches max_features; regularize_min_samples_leaf10 tested a different knob (leaf regularization) and is only invoked directionally, not claimed identical.

Targets the dominant bucket (steady_confusion, 82.3% of error rows per the champion report) with a stated, falsifiable mechanism (split-level feature starvation on a small feature set), consistent with Section 11.4's ask that mechanisms be checkable against the taxonomy after the run.
No contradiction with DOMAIN NOTES: max_features is an explicitly whitelisted ALLOWED_MODEL_PARAMS key, and nothing in the notes touches RF split-candidate sizing.

proposal.name: drop_offset_family_and_band_frac
proposal.rationale: L/R_angvel_band_frac measures energy in a fixed (0.5,3.0) Hz band that DOMAIN NOTES SS9 says is wrong for this population's slow-cadence tail (down to 0.13 Hz), so it reads near-zero for slow walkers exactly like standing and feeds steady_confusion; the prior isolated test of this drop (drop_bad_band_frac, -0.0019) ran against the un-pruned 23-feature set where RF's sqrt(23) per-split subsampling gave band_frac little chance to be chosen against the now-removed static-offset features competing for the same slots, diluting its effect, so retesting it stacked on top of the current 18-feature champion (fewer competing features, each more likely sampled per split) is a genuinely new configuration, not a repeat of the old spec.

reasons: False premise (fails check 0): rationale claims L/R_angvel_band_frac uses a (0.5,3.0) Hz band. features.py line 34 sets GAIT_BAND_HZ = (0.13, 3.0) and the comment on line 33 says this is 'deliberately NOT the healthy-adult (0.5, 3.0) Hz band' - the exact false-premise pattern this critic role exists to catch. Since the whole mechanism ('reads near-zero for slow walkers exactly like standing') depends on the band excluding slow cadence, and the real band already covers 0.13 Hz, the stated failure mode does not follow.

Any resulting F1 move cannot be attributed to the band_frac idea, which is the only actually-new piece here.

proposal.name: class_weight_balanced_subsample
proposal.rationale: BASE_MODEL_PARAMS already trains every experiment with class_weight='balanced' (weights computed once from each LORO fold's pooled y), so re-proposing 'balanced' would be a no-op; 'balanced_subsample' instead recomputes weights per tree from that tree's own bootstrap draw, which should help the minority stand class (16.9% of windows, weaker F1 0.83 vs walk's 0.96, and the source of most steady_confusion whole-segment errors) when a given tree's bootstrap happens to under-represent stand relative to the fold-wide ratio the fixed 'balanced' weight assumes.

reasons: Premise verified: stages/s2_ml/experiment.py:36-37 confirms BASE_MODEL_PARAMS already sets class_weight='balanced', so the rationale's claim that re-proposing 'balanced' would be a no-op is correct, and 'balanced_subsample' is a genuinely different, whitelisted option (experiment.py:108 lists all three).

Stand-class numbers in the rationale match the champion report exactly (812/4812=16.9% support, F1 0.83 vs 0.9641 walk), so the gap it targets is real and non-trivial (16.9% of windows, not a marginal bucket).

Not a ledger repeat: no prior entry touches class_weight; drop_features list matches the current champion's already-adopted drop_static_offset_family set, so relative to the champion baseline this is a single isolated change (class_weight only), consistent with the precedent set by max_features_full_split.
Does not contradict any DOMAIN NOTES finding (Section 9's ALLOWED_MODEL_PARAMS explicitly sanctions class_weight tuning; no established finding says balanced_subsample is a dead end).

proposal.name: more_trees_1000
proposal.rationale: steady_confusion (82% of error rows) is a whole-segment LORO generalization failure, not a boundary issue, and with only 18 features surviving the promoted static-offset-family drop, sqrt(18) selects ~4 candidate features per split so individual trees' root-level structure is more sensitive to bootstrap/feature-subsample luck than it was at 23 features; raising n_estimators from 300 to 1000 is a pure bagging-variance lever (does not change per-tree bias the way min_samples_leaf=10 or max_features=None did, both of which already failed by -0.05/-0.02) that should average out this heightened per-tree variance into a steadier ensemble vote, particularly for the minority stand class and the weakest held-out revs (rev2 0.8058).

reasons: Premise check passes: 23 total features minus the 5-feature static-offset-family drop = 18, sqrt(18)~=4.24, and n_estimators=1000 is within ALLOWED_MODEL_PARAMS bounds (10,2000) - the arithmetic in the rationale is correct.
Not a literal repeat and it is a single-parameter change (feature list is unchanged from current champion drop_static_offset_family), so novelty and attribution both pass.

Fails on leverage/evidence: steady_confusion is defined as sustained whole-segment misprediction under leave-one-rev-out - i.e. a held-out subject's windows lying systematically outside the training distribution. All trees in the forest are fit on the same training revs, so they make correlated errors on the same out-of-distribution rev regardless of how many trees are added; bagging variance reduction cannot correct a distributional-shift/bias problem, only sampling noise within one training distribution.

The ledger already has a direct test of this class of mechanism: class_weight_balanced_subsample also hypothesized a per-tree bootstrap-variance effect (there, on the minority stand class) and moved macro-F1 only +0.0020 - well below the promotion margin. Combined with min_samples_leaf=10 (-0.0549) and max_features=None (-0.0212), 3 of 3 prior model_params-only experiments show hyperparameter tuning has had negligible-to-negative effect on this dominant bucket; the proposal gives no reason n_estimators would break that pattern.
Per-rev spread (rev2 0.8058 vs rev3 0.9687) looks like a systematic per-subject bias, not tree-to-tree instability, which further undercuts the stated mechanism.

proposal.name: cap_max_depth_8
proposal.rationale: steady_confusion (82% of error rows) is a whole-segment leave-one-rev-out generalization failure, and with unconstrained max_depth (the only unexplored structural-regularization axis; min_samples_leaf=10 and max_features=None each already hurt by tuning the wrong knobs) trees can grow deep enough to carve leaves on rev-specific feature-value conjunctions rather than stopping at the shared top-level splits the importance ranking already identifies (ang_LR_corr, L/R_ang_LPF_std/ptp), so bounding depth should force every tree to rely on those broadly-shared splits and cut whole-segment misclassification on held-out subjects.

reasons: Premise verified: stages/s2_ml/experiment.py:36-37 BASE_MODEL_PARAMS has no max_depth key, so sklearn defaults to unbounded (None) - the 'unconstrained max_depth' claim holds.
Novel axis: no ledger entry has ever set model_params.max_depth; it is distinct from the two tried knobs (min_samples_leaf10, max_features=None), so not a cosmetic repeat of either.
Clean attribution: drop_features exactly matches the current champion's (drop_static_offset_family) with only model_params.max_depth=8 added - single-variable test against the live champion.
Leverage correct: targets steady_confusion, the dominant bucket (82% of error rows) per the champion report.
Feature-importance claim checks out: ang_LR_corr, L/R_ang_LPF_std/ptp are indeed the top-5 importances in the champion report.

Minor inaccuracy in rationale: max_depth is not 'the only unexplored structural-regularization axis' - ALLOWED_MODEL_PARAMS also lists min_samples_split and criterion as untried. Does not invalidate the mechanism but is an overclaim worth flagging.

Caution (not disqualifying): both prior hyperparameter-regularization attempts failed in opposite directions - min_samples_leaf=10 (more constrained, -0.0549) and max_features=None (less constrained, -0.0212) - so the pipeline's default RF complexity already looks near a local optimum. This tempers confidence the mechanism will pay off but is exactly what the metric gate, not the critic, should settle.

note: macro-F1 0.8938 vs champion 0.8977 (-0.0038); below the 0.005 promotion margin

proposal.name: drop_angvel_ptp
proposal.rationale: L_angvel_LPF_ptp/R_angvel_LPF_ptp are single-sample max-minus-min extrema on a differentiated signal (angvel = d(angle)/dt per SS4.1), so they inherit differentiation-amplified noise that std/absmean average away, matching their own low importance (L_angvel_LPF_ptp absent from the top-12, R_angvel_LPF_ptp last at 0.0237) unlike the high-importance angle-ptp features, so dropping them should shed noisy, non-transferring splits feeding steady_confusion without touching the already-validated angvel amplitude features (absmean, std).

reasons: False premise: rationale claims angvel_LPF is 'a differentiated signal (angvel = d(angle)/dt)' and that ptp on it 'inherits differentiation-amplified noise'. features.py reads L_angvel_LPF/R_angvel_LPF directly from precomputed columns (line 83, arrays built from FEATURES) - it never differentiates angle. DOMAIN NOTES SS6.2 states this explicitly: '*_angvel_LPF is LPF(Gyro) (filtered raw gyro), not d(*_ang_LPF)/dt; the two only resemble each other because Gyro == d(Deg)/dt'. SS4.6 further establishes the causality runs the other way: Deg was integrated FROM Gyro, so Gyro/angvel is the more primitive channel, not a derivative of angle. The proposed noise-amplification mechanism is backwards and contradicts recorded findings.

The empirical observation (low RF importance of L/R_angvel_LPF_ptp) is real and verified against the report, but the causal story attached to it is fabricated, not read off the code - exactly the failure Section 11.4 warns about ('a metric that moves does not confirm the mechanism claimed for it'), except here it's worse: the mechanism is wrong even before any run.

Not a repeat of any ledger entry (no prior test targeted angvel ptp specifically) and does target the dominant steady_confusion bucket in principle, but a false premise is reject regardless of downstream reasoning per review policy.

proposal.name: drop_offset_family_and_angvel_mean
proposal.rationale: L/R_angvel_LPF_mean is the window's raw signed net angular velocity, dominated by gyro zero-rate bias/drift rather than gait (SS4.1b), the same non-transferring per-device calibration artifact as the static angle-offset family the champion already drops, but the prior isolated test of dropping it (drop_angvel_mean_only, -0.0083) started from the full 23-feature set where the still-present angle-offset features were competing for split slots and diluting its effect, so stacking this drop directly on the promoted static_offset_family champion isolates whether angvel_mean is genuinely redundant bias once the angle-side bias is already gone, targeting the same steady_confusion whole-segment generalization failure.

reasons: Rationale attributes the claim 'L/R_angvel_LPF_mean is dominated by gyro zero-rate bias/drift' to SS4.1b, but SS4.1b (verified against DOMAIN_NOTES.md and features.py) is only about gyro unit inconsistency (deg/s vs rad/s) and the Deg<->Gyro axis permutation - it says nothing about zero-rate bias or drift. No section in DOMAIN NOTES establishes a gyro zero-rate-bias finding for angvel_LPF. This is the same failure mode the false-premise check exists to catch: a mechanism is asserted and cited to a section that does not support it.

The core mechanism was already measured, not hypothesized: drop_angvel_mean_only tested dropping these exact two features and macro-F1 fell -0.0083 - the opposite of what a 'pure non-transferring bias artifact' predicts (removing dead weight should help or be neutral, not hurt). The proposal's 'diluted by competing offset features' explanation for reversing that result is asserted, not evidenced - no measurement in the ledger or report supports that stacking flips the sign.

Feature-importance table for the current champion doesn't even surface angvel_mean-type raw-mean terms in the top 12 (std/ptp/absmean/corr/dom_hz dominate) - there's no importance-based case that this pair is driving the 82%-share steady_confusion bucket the way ang_LR_offset/ang mean/absmean were shown to.

proposal.name: drop_angvel_lr_corr
proposal.rationale: angvel_LR_corr correlates two differentiation-derived gyro channels (angvel = d(angle)/dt per SS4.1, a tight but noise-amplifying relationship already used to reject the angvel ptp features), so it is a noisier duplicate of the already-dominant ang_LR_corr (top-4 importance, computed on the smoother, non-differentiated angle channel) and likely lets RF split on session-specific noise in that redundant copy rather than transferable antiphase signal, feeding steady_confusion (82% of error rows) under leave-one-rev-out.

reasons: False premise, directly checkable against the champion report itself: the rationale claims angvel ptp features were 'already used to reject' as noise-amplifying duplicates, but R_angvel_LPF_ptp appears live in the champion's top-12 feature importance table (0.0237) - it was never dropped, so the cited precedent doesn't exist.

Rationale inverts the causality Section 4.6 established: it calls angvel 'differentiation-derived' from the 'smoother, non-differentiated' angle channel, but 4.6 explicitly corrects this - Deg (angle) is the on-sensor fusion output integrated FROM Gyro; Gyro/angvel is the more primitive transducer channel, not a noisier derivative of angle. The proposal's core noise-amplification argument runs backwards against a named, dated domain-notes correction.
No ledger entry tests angvel_LR_corr in isolation, so the idea itself isn't a repeat, but it's built on a broken mechanism, not a verified one - not approvable as-is.
